title: Google Photos Magic Editor: GenAI Under the Hood of a Billion-User App - Kelvin Ma, Google Photos
talk_summary: Kelvin Ma describes Google Photos' shift from on-device ML editing to server-side GenAI Magic Editor, emphasizing evals, constrained use cases, and orchestration of specialized models. He argues AI engineering must reduce model randomness with benchmarks, smaller models, and deterministic software.

takeaways.technique: Benchmark as unit tests for models
takeaways.what_they_do: They maintain a benchmark that reflects real-world usage and use it to decide whether a new model is actually better before shipping.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the benchmark is the equivalent of unit testing for your model and you need to maintain it

takeaways.what_they_do: Once a large model proves useful in production, they replace it with a smaller, faster, or more efficient model, including traditional non-ML code where possible.
takeaways.evidence_quote: replace with a smaller model, faster model, more efficient model

takeaways.technique: System of specialized models and tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Magic Eraser is not one model: it detects distractors, segments them, inpaints, and renders with custom GL for a seamless result.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We are detecting distractors. We are segmenting them. We are then running an impainter on them

takeaways.technique: Recorded fixtures for expensive model tests
takeaways.what_they_do: Large models cannot run in daily automated regression suites, so they discuss recapturing responses or using test servers rather than live model calls in every test.
takeaways.evidence_quote: these models are way too big. We can't run them in our automated testing suite for our daily regressions

takeaways.what_they_do: They reduce ambiguity across product, research, and UX by narrowing broad GenAI goals into specific user use cases that can be engineered and evaluated.
takeaways.evidence_quote: anything is possible means nothing is out of scope, which means you cannot design an engineering system around it

takeaways.technique: Prompt is a bug, not a feature
takeaways.what_they_do: They extract user intent and guide users through constrained UX rather than making users write detailed prompts for every edit.
takeaways.evidence_quote: prompt is a bug, not a feature
